title: Root-cause spotlight dashboard: latency by request-shape and IO-boundary
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a ‘Root-cause Spotlight’ dashboard that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route with a primary cohorting dimension of request-shape (short/medium/long token windows) and an IO-boundary marker that splits streaming vs non-streaming requests. Unlike our other dashboards which focus on slices by route or percentile only, this board is optimized for fast investigation of tail regressions by correlating latency spikes with runtime signals (kernel version, KV cache hit, batching size, node type, and region) and linking into traces from a single click.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for each model x route tile with separate bars/lines for streaming and non-streaming
Request-shape bucketing applied (<=32 tokens, 33-256, >256) with ability to customize the buckets via a dropdown
Each tile includes small inline heatmap of kernel-version vs latency percentile and a checkbox to overlay KV cache hit ratio
Clicking any percentile opens a trace sampler that links to the trace with the request-id and highlights KV cache decisions and batching size
Panels refresh within 30s and have stable query cost - histogram-to-percentile transform implemented in metrics pipeline
Onboarded to console release console-2026.03 and has alerting rules for sustained p95 breach by model-route-io-mode
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Scoped initial PRD and example mockups (see links). Goal is to reduce mean time to root cause for tail spikes from hours to <30 minutes.

2026-03-11 Marco Ruiz: Started metric work - added percentile transforms to the metrics pipeline and new histogram buckets for inference latency. Observed that current sampling of traces (1%) is too low for tail analysis; proposing adaptive sampling when p95 > SLO.

2026-03-11 Design feedback (Lina Gomez): Mockup should surface an IO boundary toggle prominently, and show request-shape legend. Suggest compact sparklines per tile instead of full-time-series to keep board density high.
2026-03-12 PR #7123 opened: dashboard JSON + metrics transform + small change to trace hook to include kernel_version and kv_cache_hit tags. Requesting review from telemetry and runtime teams.

2026-03-12 Telemetry review (Rajiv): OK on transforms, but need to ensure metric cardinality bounded: kernel_version should be mapped to a small set (v1/v2/quantized) in the pipeline. Also recommended pre-aggregate KV hit ratio at 1m.
2026-03-12 Next: implement adaptive trace sampling and add alerting rules; follow up with Dedicated team for node-type tagging availability.
notes: Implementation details: Use histogram quantile transforms in the metrics pipeline and emit p50/p95/p99 at 1m granularity. Add a lightweight metric kv_cache_hit_ratio aggregated per model/route/node_type.
Trace linking: enrich span root with tags {request_id, model, route, io_mode, kernel_version, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, node_type}. Ensure sample keys include p95 triggers.
Alerting: p95 > X ms for 5m => warn, 15m => page; breakouts by model-route-io_mode to reduce noise.
acceptance_test_steps: Deploy dashboard to staging and validate tiles for 5 active models with synthetic workload across streaming and non-streaming clients
Inject synthetic tail latency (introduce sleep in runtime) and confirm p95 jump surfaces and trace links contain kernel_version and kv_cache_hit tags
Verify alert fires only for sustained breaches and not for single-request spikes
